chapter: Part Two: theaters and the Chicago scene
title: The Villa Venice band's repertoire
summary: Stocks and symphonic arrangements mixed with faked New Orleans tunes.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: That band you were telling me about that you were with at the Villa Venice, with Freddie Keppard and Bechet.
I sure would have liked to have heard that band.

Oh, boy, that was a great band. We played a lot of stocks and big symphonic arrangements, they called them. Special arrangements. It was put out by the publishers. We called them symphonic arrangements. We had a lot of those, and small stocks.
But did they play any of the New Orleans tunes? You know, Bechet and --
Do you recall any of the tunes that you might play? Was this sort of, you know, the standard Dixieland repertoire?
Yeah, sort of standard. You know, like "Panama," and all the standard Dixieland tunes.
Later you made an arrangement of "Wolverine Blues" for Earl's band that was very nice.
